title: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus)
what: The surgeon cuts and realigns the bone at the base of the big toe. The bone is held with screws or staples, and the toe sits straighter.
why: When the bunion hurts and makes walking and finding shoes hard, and comfortable shoes and insoles do not help.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours; usually 1 to 2 days in hospital, or home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Diabetes and circulation problems in the legs
If you smoke. It slows bone healing

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Set up a comfortable spot at home. You will walk very little for the first weeks. Ask if you need crutches.

bring: A wide shoe for your other foot
steps: On the day, you change, and an IV line is placed
The anesthetist gives general anesthesia or numbs the leg
The surgeon makes a cut on the foot and realigns the bone
The bone is held with screws or a plate
The wound is stitched, and the foot is bandaged
You get a special post-op shoe
feel: For the first days, the foot hurts and swells. You will get painkillers
Heaviness and a tight bandage are normal
Walking in the special shoe feels strange
after: Keep your foot raised. It reduces swelling and pain
You usually walk in the special shoe for about 4 to 6 weeks
Keep the bandage dry until your doctor says it is OK
Regular shoes when your surgeon allows
red_flags: Severe pain, swelling, and pain in the calf of either leg
Toes turn blue, cold, or numb
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or pus or a smell from under the bandage
Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: Will the screws stay in for life?
faq.a: Usually yes. They do not get in the way. They are only removed if they bother you.

faq.q: When can I wear regular shoes?
faq.a: Usually after 6 to 8 weeks, based on an X-ray and your surgeon's decision.

reminders.text: Foot surgery tomorrow. Bring your documents, medicines, and a wide shoe. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
